  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  NOVEMBER 2, 2021

1.  CHAIR ZUCKERMAN called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Zuckerman, Boothe, Brown Schachter, Lum,
  Munday, Romanelli, Scott, Varner

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Combs, Martin

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  Deputy Bouse, LA County Sheriff’s Department

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, AUGUST 17,
  2021.

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  AUGUST 17, 2021.

AYES:  Zuckerman, Boothe, Brown Schachter, Lum, Munday, Romanelli, Scott, Varner

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  MASONGATE DRIVE/SUGARHILL DRIVE AT FERNCREEK DRIVE – REQUEST TO
  REMOVE STOP SIGNS

Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy provided a presentation summarizing the staff report.
Traffic volume counts were collected on Tuesday, October 5, 2021 for a 24 hr. period at the
intersections at Masongate Drive, Sugarhill Drive, and Ferncreek Drive. Deputy Itagaki stated that
when looking to install any traffic control device, the California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control
Devices (CAMUTCD) is used. Stop and yield signs are intended to provide direction for right-of-
way at an intersection and they are not to be used for speed control. When looking at installing
stop signs it also requires review and analysis of traffic count data, visibility of an intersection, and
reported collision history. Deputy Itagaki stated that no records were found to determine the
reason that these stop signs were installed.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the CAMUTCD does not provide specific guidelines
for removal of stop signs. However, the removal of signs should be considered with utmost care;
the removal of stop signs are of particular concern since this could result in increased accident
frequency. If this intersection were studied using the current guidelines, the traffic counts would
not satisfy the guidelines for multi-way or all-way stop signs to be installed.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that due to the favorable collision history, the
intersection of Masongate Drive, Sugarhill Drive at Ferncreek Drive appears to provide the

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, November 2, 2021
 appropriate right-of-way guidance for vehicles travelling through these intersections and stated
that staff would not be in favor of removing the stop signs.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the all-way stop controls at
Masongate Drive, Sugarhill Drive, and Ferncreek Drive remain in place at this time.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that the reason she requested that this item be
discussed is that everyday drivers speed past the stop sign and asked what can be done for
drivers to stop at the stop sign. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki suggested reminding residents
about the stop sign through the HOA and/or request that the Sheriff’s Department do selective
enforcement in the area. Deputy Bouse confirmed that she will put in a request to have traffic
enforcement monitor the stop sign.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE asked if there are other traffic calming measures that can be
put into place. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki suggested increasing the size of the stop sign
and/or adding a “stop ahead” sign, particularly on Sugarhill Drive and Masongate Drive.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT inquired about the request to remove the signs. COMMITTEE
MEMBER BOOTHE stated that at the last meeting she mentioned that the stop signs give a false
sense of security to pedestrians and drivers are speeding through them with no repercussions.
COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT mentioned that people tend to ignore traffic control devices that
do not make sense to them.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that in his neighborhood, they have utilized the city’s
speed board to help with speeding issues. This can be requested by contacting Mike Goldsmith,
Maintenance Superintendent.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki also suggested to refresh the painting of the limit line and stop
markings.

Staff received four email correspondence after the agenda was published in opposition of the
removal of the stop signs. These were forwarded to the Traffic and Safety Committee prior to the
meeting.

William Cook, Resident suggested installing speed humps. (Comment via chat feature on Zoom)

Director Wahba stated that the installation of speed humps would require a vote of 50% plus one
of residents. The request would need to be initiated by the homeowners’ association. However,
he stated that once drivers get accustomed to them, they speed through them and cause more
noise than speed control.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT asked if rumble strips could be an option. Traffic Engineering
Deputy Itagaki expressed her concern with installing them near residences due to the noise that
they produce.

Mr. Cook stated that the stop sign was installed in about 1976. He stated that Sugarhill Drive has
a bit of a blind curve and the stop sign was installed to control traffic on Ferncreek Drive from
drivers coming from Sugarhill Drive. At one time there was a 15mph limit on Masongate Drive.
Mr. Cook stated that he lives where the street curves and the stop sign is helpful for him to be
able to back out of his driveway safely. The number of families with young children has increased
in the neighborhood, there are also people riding horses, and people on bicycles. Mr. Cook stated
that he is strongly opposed to the removal of the stop sign and added that periodic enforcement
would be helpful.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT
to,
  LEAVE THE STOP SIGNS IN THEIR CURRENT LOCATION. INCREASE THE SIZE OF
  THE STOP SIGNS AND REPAINT THE STREET MARKINGS.

AYES:  Zuckerman, Boothe, Brown Schachter, Lum, Munday, Romanelli, Scott, Varner
NOES:
ABSENT:  Combs, Martin
ABSTAIN:

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, November 2, 2021
 There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

B.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AT 3739 TO 3815 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH –
  REQUEST TO ADD NO U-TURN SIGN

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation summarizing the staff report. Data was
collected on turning movement counts in the PM peak hours since this is the time when eastbound
Palos Verdes Drive North (PVDN) is most congested. The collision history for a four and a half-
year period was provided and there were no collisions at “no name” street and Palos Verdes Drive
North.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the installation of “No U-Turn” signs on Palos
Verdes Drive North at 3739 to 3815 Palos Verdes Drive North could impact other intersections on
Palos Verdes Drive North since vehicles wanting the execute U-Turns will likely go further up the
street and use another location to make a U-Turn.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety
Committee discuss the concern regarding eastbound U-turns. It is further recommended the
Committee receive public testimony and provide direction to staff regarding the matter.

Staff received an e-comment from Jeremy Alonzo, which Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki read
to the committee.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER stated that there are “No U-Turn” signs at
Ranchview and yet drivers still make U-Turns and added that people will see the signs and back
into Palos Verdes Drive North. COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER stated that adding
the sign may be more dangerous and people will find alternatives.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT asked why drivers are making the U-Turn at this particular
location. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that this may be the place where traffic begins
to back-up during peak hours.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE
MEMBER LUM to,

  NOT ESTABLISH “NO U-TURN” SIGNS ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AT 3739
  TO 3815 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

C.  DRAFT LOCAL ROADWAY SAFETY PLAN – STAKEHOLDERS INPUT

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki introduced Nicolle Spann and Emilio Murga with Willdan who
provided a presentation on the Draft Local Roadway Safety Plan (LRSP). The City was awarded
funds to create and analyze collisions throughout the city, which is part of the LRSP.

This is a tool that the State uses to look at Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) funds.
If the City is looking to apply for funds from the Highway Safety Improvement Program, a LRSP
is required.

Nicolle Spann provided a presentation overview of what an LRSP is, citywide collision trends in
the City, and an overview of the two types of HSIP projects – Benefit Cost-to-Ratio (BCR) projects
and Set-aside projects.

Mr. Murga provided an overview of the proposed projects, which include:

  •  Citywide Guardrail Set-Aside Project - citywide upgrades to existing guardrails
  •  Downtown Business Corridor Pedestrian Set-Aside Project – upgrade crossings with
  beacons and push buttons at (4) crossings on Deep Valley Drive
  •  Intersection Lighting BCR Project – install intersection lighting at (4) non-signalized
  intersections
  •  Traffic Signal Improvement BCR Project – upgrade signal hardware and provide
  advanced detection at (7) intersections on Silver Spur and Hawthorne Blvd.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  3
Minutes, November 2, 2021
   •  PVDN Traffic Signal Improvement BCR Project – upgrade signal hardware and provide
  advanced detection at (5) intersections on PVDN

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that some of the traffic signals for the intersections
included in the PVDN Traffic Signal Improvement Project, have already been improved/upgraded
in the past five years and asked what would be improved upon. Mr. Murga stated that the traffic
signals could be upgraded to add yellow reflective back plates, which makes the signal more
visible from greater distances; upgrade the lenses to make them clearer; and changing the
location of the mountings.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER commented that Ranchview was included in the
Citywide Guardrail Project and this particular guardrail was replaced within the last five years and
has not seen any damage to it. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that the comments from
this meeting will be noted. The various locations will be reviewed again before finalizing the report
for funding. There are new standards for guardrails, that may include the height.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT asked if there is any science on the yellow reflective back plates.
COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that it is used for AI on electric/self-driving vehicles.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN asked about any cost sharing for the portion of Crenshaw Blvd. where the
City does not have full ownership. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki the City will be applying
under their own application, but staff can look into asking the County to join.

In response to a question from CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, Ms. Spann stated that $1M is available to
each jurisdiction for set-aside projects during each HSIP cycles, which is every two years.

Ms. Spann also clarified that jurisdictions can apply for Set-aside projects and BCR projects and
stated that applying for all of the proposed projects would still be under the maximum threshold.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY expressed his concern with adding more lighting to
intersections and stated that staff may need more input from residents.

A brief discussion ensued on the Intersection Lighting Project.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that from the discussion, it is apparent that the
Intersection Lighting Project should be removed from the list of projects at this time and can be
revisited in the future.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT expressed his concern with the roadway curves on Silver Spur
Road at Marina Drive.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that there may be a need for additional lighting on Silver
Arrow and Drybank Drive area for the Commercial District. Mr. Murga stated that he will look into
the collision history in the area and this could be added to the list, if it qualifies.

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A.  TRAFFIC CONGESTION AT RANCHO VISTA SCHOOL

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI provided a presentation with concerns regarding traffic
congestion at Rancho Vista School and Dapplegray Elementary. The long lines of vehicles in the
morning and afternoon hours impacts the flow of traffic on westbound and eastbound lanes on
Palos Verdes Drive North. The area where the vehicles are lined up or parked to go into Rancho
Vista School are the westerly side of Palos Verdes Drive North at Moccasin Lane, Palos Verdes
Lane, and Silver Saddle Road. At Dapplegray Elementary, a similar situation occurs on the
westbound lane of Palos Verdes Drive North.

COMMITTEE ROMANELLI stated that this was discussed at Los Ranchos Verdes HOA meeting
and provided potential areas of improvement. Some of the suggestions include, adding
supervision before 8:15 a.m. and bussing kids using environmentally friendly vehicles.
Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  4
Minutes, November 2, 2021
 COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that Dapplegray Elementary has a road that goes
around the school where parents’ vehicles could line up. This would involve working with the
school district.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN stated that there are a lot of improvements being made on Palos Verdes
Drive North that may impact the situation and he would be interested in seeing if the timing that
the traffic conductor is scheduled at the school may be a solution. CHAIR ZUCKERMAN
suggested that staff may be able to look at this and report back to the Traffic and Safety
Committee.

COMMITTEE MEMBER SCOTT stated that he is not sure there is a solution to the situation at
Rancho Vista School, but he is not opposed to putting this item on a future agenda for discussion.
In regards to Dapplegray Elementary, they do have a long road around the school that is marked
for drop-off and pick-up and believes that the backup on Palos Verdes Drive North may be due to
parents who do not want to get in line and rather drop-off ahead of the driveway.

COMMITTEE MEMBER LUM stated that over the years the intersection at Rancho Vista has been
looked at many times and having the crossing guard and the traffic deputy at the intersection has
been effective. Director Wahba stated that there are too many people driving their kids to school,
another solution may be to stagger start times, but this may prolong the congestion in the area.
For Dapplegray Elementary, there is a grant to widen Palos Verdes Drive North in the area and
this should help.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROMANELLI stated that there is no one at the school prior to 8:15 am
and if there was a home room for kids to wait at 7:30 am, this would help so that kids could be
dropped off earlier. Director Wahba stated that there is a “Kids Corner” program, which is a before
school program, but there is a cost associated with this program. Deputy Bouse stated that due
to COVID, no kids can be on campus prior to 8:15 am since kids need to show negative tests.
This has also impacted traffic and hopefully next year when the restrictions are lifted, things will
improve.

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN suggested speaking with PV Transit about their bus stop locations.
Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she would review COMMITTEE MEMBER
ROMANELLI’S presentation to see if there is any options for solutions that could be brought back
for discussion at a future committee meeting.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER asked when the three-rail vinyl fencing on Palos
Verdes Drive North outside of City Hall would be repaired. Director Wahba stated that there may
be issues getting the same type of fencing, but he will check with Mike Goldsmith, Maintenance
Superintendent and report back via email.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MUNDAY stated that he is receiving complaints with concerns about
pedestrian crossing issues at Silver Spur and Palos Verdes Drive North. He stated that he will
come in to speak with Director Wahba on the specifics of the issues at that intersection.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the meeting at 8:19 p.m.
